**SOCIETY SCOOP: British Aristocrat Kirsty Everett Ties the Knot with Renowned Philanthropist Ann Elizabeth Badger**

In a private ceremony held at the picturesque Everett Estate in the English countryside, Lady Kirsty Everett, a member of the esteemed British peerage, exchanged vows with Ann Elizabeth Badger, a respected philanthropist and humanitarian. The union, which took place on a crisp autumn morning, marks a new chapter in the lives of the two women, who have been inseparable for over a decade. According to sources close to the family, the intimate gathering was attended by a select group of friends, family members, and dignitaries, including several prominent figures from the world of politics and charity work. The ceremony was officiated by the Reverend James Thompson, a longtime friend of the Everett family. Lady Kirsty, 35, is the daughter of the 12th Earl of Wiltshire and has been actively involved in various charitable initiatives throughout her life. Her philanthropic work has focused primarily on education and women's empowerment, earning her recognition and respect within the British aristocracy. Ann Elizabeth Badger, 78, is a renowned philanthropist and humanitarian, known for her tireless efforts in supporting marginalized communities around the world. Her organization, the Badger Foundation, has provided critical aid and resources to disaster-stricken areas and underserved populations. In an exclusive interview with our publication, Lady Kirsty expressed her joy and gratitude, saying, "Ann has been my rock, my partner, and my best friend for many years. I feel incredibly fortunate to have found someone who shares my values and passion for making a positive impact in the world." Ann Elizabeth Badger added, "Kirsty brings a sense of purpose and energy to my life that I never thought possible. I'm thrilled to start this new chapter with the love of my life." The couple's union has been met with widespread support and congratulations from their peers and the general public alike. "This is a wonderful day for both Kirsty and Ann," said Lady Victoria Windsor, a close friend of the couple. "They are a perfect match, and I have no doubt that their love and commitment to each other will only continue to grow stronger." According to data from the UK Office for National Statistics, same-sex marriages have seen a significant increase in recent years, with over 10,000 ceremonies taking place in 2022 alone.
